reading.body:
EleutherAI is a nonprofit that builds open training and evaluation infrastructure, not compute infrastructure, so its constraints are funding and data rather than power.

The organization's output is the layer above the grid: datasets like the Pile and Common Pile, the GPT-NeoX training framework, the LM Evaluation Harness, and the Pythia model suites released with training data, code, and intermediate checkpoints. Its stated aim is to let researchers without frontier-lab resources do frontier work. That places it on the demand side of compute, consuming capacity it does not own, and on the supply side of the tools that make limited capacity more useful.

Its safety work is shaped by the same position. Deep Ignorance filters hazardous material out of pretraining data, and the Open-Weight Pretraining Safety Accelerator with FAR.AI targets safety that survives public weights. Both assume models will be released rather than gated, which is a different bet from labs that treat weights as controlled infrastructure.

The data does not cover funding, headcount, compute providers, or energy use, so it cannot show how much capacity EleutherAI actually consumes or where it runs. It also lists no products and no cases, so the record describes stated work and released artifacts, not deployment or revenue.
